description: The plot illustrates how accuracy varies with initial confidence for three series shown as colored lines with markers and error bars. The x-axis is labeled “Initial Confidence,” uses a linear scale, and spans from 0.91 to 0.98 with tick labels at 0.01 intervals. The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy,” uses a linear scale, and ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 with labeled ticks at 0.2 intervals. One series is a blue solid line with circular markers; it starts near 0.85 accuracy at initial confidence 0.91, rises to about 1.00 at 0.92, and then stays close to 0.98–1.00 through 0.98 (ending around 1.00). A second series is an orange dashed line with diamond markers; it begins around 0.63 at 0.91, increases to about 0.92 at 0.92, then decreases across the remaining x-values to roughly 0.08 at 0.98, with intermediate points around 0.80 (0.93), 0.73 (0.94), 0.56 (0.95), 0.35 (0.96), and 0.21 (0.97). The third series is a green dash-dot line with square markers; it starts around 0.21 at 0.91, dips to about 0.07 at 0.92, then increases steadily to approximately 0.90 by 0.98, passing through about 0.16 (0.93), 0.23 (0.94), 0.42 (0.95), 0.63 (0.96), and 0.75 (0.97). Each point includes vertical error bars indicating variability around the plotted accuracy values.
